# Things to NEVER do

> **Permanent rules.** Every agent reads this before producing output. These are the absolute "do not" list — distinct from one-time mistakes (which live in [mistakes.md](mistakes.md)). Rules here propagate to every agent via `shared:user_preferences:dont:*` keys in agent_memory.

---

## Writing style (enforced by Humanizer skill)

- **NEVER use em dashes** (—). Switch to commas, parens, or hyphens. Em dashes are the loudest AI-tell in Tony's experience.
- **NEVER use these banned words**: delve, landscape, pivotal, crucial, leverage, streamline, empower, foster, robust, cutting-edge, holistic, synergy, paradigm. These signal AI-generated text.
- **NEVER use these banned phrases**: "Great question!", "I hope this finds you well", "Let's dive in", "It's important to note", "It's worth noting that", "As an AI assistant", "I'm here to help"
- **NEVER use sycophantic openings** — no "Great point!", no "Absolutely!", no "What an interesting question!"
- **NEVER cycle synonyms** — pick one term and stick to it (don't write "leverage X to drive Y to harness Z to enable…")
- **NEVER write the rule of three** unless there are genuinely three things — "fast, reliable, scalable" when only two of those are true is AI-slop
- **NEVER use emojis in business writing** — only the 🔷 sigil is permitted, only at signing-off lines

## Communication rules

- **NEVER auto-send to external recipients.** Drafts only. Tony reviews, Tony sends. Earn the autonomy over 50 right answers, not on day one.
- **NEVER identify yourself as AI** in external-facing content (emails, proposals, decks). No "as an AI assistant", no "generated by Dust", no "I'm an automated system".
- **NEVER post on weekends.** Held until Monday 8 AM CET unless explicitly requested.
- **NEVER send pricing tier first.** Confirm budget envelope before any tier framing. See [[../_wiki/patterns/pricing-response-budget-envelope-first]].

## Content + research rules

- **NEVER fabricate data.** Flag uncertainty: "Confidence: MEDIUM — based on [source]." Never present an inferred number as a verified one.
- **NEVER cite a number you can't trace.** If the source isn't in `input_context_refs:`, don't include the number.
- **NEVER promote confidential agent output to public canonical.** Sensitivity gate enforces (see [[../_wiki/fleet-architecture/sensitivity-gate]]).
- **NEVER touch Tony's off-limits topics**: NDA-bound client deals, active M&A negotiations, salary data, performance reviews, HR matters. List maintained in agent registry `forbidden_strings:` field per confidential agent.

## Cost discipline rules (Rule 0)

- **NEVER silently switch from Sonnet to Opus.** Default model is `claude-sonnet-4-6`. Opus is opt-in via `/think-build` or explicit subagent invocation.
- **NEVER burn Opus on execution.** If Edit/Write is being called while active model is Opus, that's a violation. Re-route through a Sonnet subagent.
- **NEVER skip the seven-step loop** for non-trivial work. THINK → PLAN → BUILD → REVIEW → TEST → SHIP → REFLECT.

## Architecture rules (the audit-winning ones)

- **NEVER bypass the SBAP triage.** Every Dust agent write goes to `00_Inbox/from-dust/<agent>/<date>-<slug>.md` with valid frontmatter. Skipping = no learnings accumulate = the loop breaks.
- **NEVER hand-edit `_brain_api/canonical/` or `_brain_index/`.** They're generated. Use `/promote-pattern` to create canonical blocks.
- **NEVER skip the wiki layer.** Every Dust agent reads `_wiki/<their-domain>/` BEFORE crafting output. The wiki is the LLM-maintained memory — bypassing it means rediscovering what's already known.
- **NEVER edit `_wiki/methodology/` automatically.** Block-curator proposes, Tony approves. Methodology is Tony-stable.

## Tone rules per audience

- **For external client communication**: short sentences, concrete specifics, contractions OK, no corporate jargon. Match the brand DNA (`03_Resources/PowerPoint Standards/Brand DNA.md`).
- **For internal Mantu communication**: more casual, contractions, opinions welcome.
- **For Tony directly**: skip the warm-up. State the thing. Confidence levels explicit when relevant.

## What "good" looks like (the inverse list — for reference)

- Concrete specifics over abstract claims
- One coherent thought per paragraph
- The Apple-keynote standing-ovation test: "would this earn applause?"
- The "five-year-old test" for explanations
- Brevity over thoroughness when the audience is busy (Tony, executives, procurement teams)

---

🔷 *Permanent rules · Tony's correction loop populates this · 2026-05-17*

---

## Distribution (how these rules reach every tool)

| Tool | Read mechanism | Write-back mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | SessionStart hook + `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` contract | SessionEnd capture + block-curator nightly |
| Codex | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` VAULT MEMORY CONTRACT | same contract, manual append to mistakes.md |
| Gemini / Antigravity | `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` VAULT MEMORY CONTRACT (paste into Antigravity rules UI too) | same contract |
| Dust agents | playbook READ PROTOCOL step 0 | SBAP `learnings`/`mistakes_to_avoid` frontmatter -> triage -> block-curator |

Added 2026-06-04 by the Mission Control build.

---

## Lessons discipline (added 2026-06-05)

- **Maintain [[Lessons|Lessons.md]].** Every time we hit an issue, root-cause it, fix it → add a numbered lesson (Issue N: Symptom · Root cause · Fix/Rule · Saves), newest on top. Skim it before debugging anything Obsidian/plugin/agent-related so we never re-pay the same token cost.
- **Efficiency first** (Lessons L-E1..E4): verify in one CDP pass not N reloads · `node --check` ≠ loads (do a module-load test) · grep-then-read tight windows, don't re-read whole files · memoize heavy scans.

---

## Build estimates are mandatory (added 2026-06-07)

- **ALWAYS give a token + time (+ cost) estimate before building anything non-trivial.** Tony requires this as a *fundamental*, not an afterthought — when scoping/planning ANY project, report the projected **tokens · time · cost** (a range is fine: best→worst case) so he knows the scope before committing to the expensive work. WALTEUR emits this to `walteur-kit/estimate.json` right after PLAN; carry the same habit into every build/plan, regardless of tooling.

When you notice a mistake, append a new section below using this template:

```
## YYYY-MM-DD — <agent> — <one-line summary>

**What happened:** [1-2 sentences on what the agent did wrong]
**Why it was wrong:** [the actual harm or wrong-result]
**Root cause:** [what assumption / data / logic failed]
**The correction:** [what to do instead — link to dont.md rule or canonical block]
**Propagation:** [where this is now enforced — Humanizer skill / dont.md / canonical block / agent playbook]

```

Block-curator distills agent SBAP `mistakes_to_avoid:` arrays into this file nightly when n_observations ≥ 1.

---

## Mistakes captured so far

### 2026-05-17 — claude-code (meta) — Haiku classifier hook misfired on conversational prompts

**What happened:** The UserPromptSubmit hook had a Haiku classifier intended to enforce Rule 0 by recommending `/think-build` for non-trivial requests. It kept misfiring on conversational prompts ("hey", "thanks", "what's the time"), suggesting `/think-build` when no work was happening.

**Why it was wrong:** Created friction in chat flow, undermined trust in the classifier, increased perceived AI clunkiness.

**Root cause:** Haiku-class model is too eager to suggest action even for greetings. The prompt couldn't be hardened past 5 iterations.

**The correction:** Removed the classifier hook entirely from `~/.claude/settings.json`. Rule 0 still enforced via three other mechanisms — Sonnet default + Builder Logic + `/think-build` skill.

**Propagation:** Settings.json updated. Documented in `99_Meta/fleet-audit-2026-05-17.md` (audit v3 → v4 transition).

---

### 2026-05-17 — triage_dust_writes.py — YAML datetime parsed to datetime object, broke JSON Schema validation

**What happened:** PyYAML auto-parses ISO date strings into datetime objects. JSON Schema validator wanted strings. SBAP validation failed on perfectly valid Dust agent writes.

**Why it was wrong:** Good writes got rejected to `99_Meta/dust-errors.log`, learnings didn't accumulate, the fleet looked broken when the protocol was fine.

**Root cause:** Default PyYAML behavior + jsonschema strict mode mismatch.

**The correction:** Added `_coerce_for_schema()` helper in `triage_dust_writes.py` that walks the parsed frontmatter and converts datetime back to ISO strings before validation.

**Propagation:** Patched in the canonical triage script. Documented in `99_Meta/dust-write-log.md`.

---

### 2026-05-17 — graph_sync.py — f-string backslash in Python 3.9

**What happened:** A code line tried to format a Windows path inside an f-string with an embedded backslash escape. Python 3.9 doesn't allow backslashes inside f-string expressions.

**Why it was wrong:** Build broke on machines running Python 3.9; only worked on 3.10+.

**Root cause:** Python 3.9 grammar restriction.

**The correction:** Pre-compute the escaped value outside the f-string into a variable, then reference the variable inside the f-string.

**Propagation:** Patched in `graph_sync.py`. Added to coding-behavior-contract notes about f-string portability.

---

### 2026-05-17 — triage-watcher.sh + Python — lock collision between bash and Python

**What happened:** The triage-watcher bash wrapper acquired a flock, then exec'd into the Python watcher. The Python watcher tried to re-acquire its own lock on the same file. Collision = neither could run.

**Why it was wrong:** Real-time triage silently stopped working. Symptoms: agent writes piled up in `00_Inbox/from-dust/` without being processed.

**Root cause:** Two-process lock-coordination is racy and unnecessary when one process exec'es into the other.

**The correction:** Removed the bash-side flock when handing off to Python via exec. Python owns the lock; bash just kicks off Python.

**Propagation:** Patched in `~/AI-Brain-build/scripts/triage-watcher.sh`. Documented as a coding-behavior-contract note about exec'ing into Python from bash.

---

### 2026-05-17 — Mantu tenant blocks Microsoft Graph public app_id (AADSTS65002)

**What happened:** Attempted to use Microsoft's public sample app_id for Graph integration. Mantu's tenant rejected with AADSTS65002 (admin consent required for tenant).

**Why it was wrong:** Wasted exploration time chasing a path the tenant doesn't allow.

**Root cause:** Mantu IT policy — no third-party Graph apps without explicit admin registration.

**The correction:** Deferred Graph integration entirely. Document at `99_Meta/graph-integration-deferred.md`. Architecture redesigned to use OneDrive connector exclusively (the SBAP transport).

**Propagation:** Documented in onboarding's "Definitively NOT available" list (Phase 0). Deployment constraint baked in: never recommend new MCPs.

---

### 2026-05-17 — KeyError on stats.json bump in triage script

**What happened:** First-time agent stats bump errored with KeyError when the `by_day` dict didn't have today's entry yet.

**Why it was wrong:** Triage crashed on first write for new agents, leaving the write half-processed.

**Root cause:** Missing setdefault pattern.

**The correction:** Used `setdefault(today_iso, 0)` for the by_day dict before incrementing.

**Propagation:** Patched in `triage_dust_writes.py`.

---

## Patterns emerging from the mistakes log

Block-curator surfaces patterns when 3+ entries share a theme:

- **Lock coordination**: triage-watcher + Python collision; potential pattern if more lock issues emerge → would promote to `_wiki/fleet-architecture/lock-coordination.md`
- **Python version portability**: f-string 3.9 issue; potential pattern if more 3.9-vs-3.10 issues emerge → would promote to coding-behavior-contract addendum
- **External-service rejection**: Microsoft Graph AADSTS65002; potential pattern if more tenant-rejection issues emerge → would promote to `_wiki/fleet-architecture/tenant-restrictions.md`

---

🔷 *Mistakes log · history kept forever · block-curator never deletes · 2026-05-17*

## 2026-06-04 — claude-code — Hand-authored Obsidian workspace tree silently dropped the terminal pane

- **What went wrong**: Wrote `.obsidian/workspaces.json` + `workspace.json` from a hand-built layout tree; Obsidian's deserializer normalized the file and silently discarded the `terminal:terminal` leaf. Delivered as "done" after JSON validation only — JSON-valid is not Obsidian-valid.
- **Why**: Trusted schema reconstruction over the application's own serializer; no live-app verification before claiming success.
- **The correction**: Always patch leaves into Obsidian's OWN serialized `workspace.json` (quit app → edit → relaunch → read back the rewritten file to confirm the leaf survived). GUI-state claims require read-back verification, not file-write verification.

# /graphify

Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection, an honest audit trail, and three outputs: interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a plain-language GRAPH_REPORT.md.

## Usage

```
/graphify                                             # full pipeline on current directory → Obsidian vault
/graphify <path>                                      # full pipeline on specific path
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>           # clone repo then run full pipeline on it
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --branch <branch>  # clone a specific branch
/graphify <url1> <url2> ...                           # clone multiple repos, build each, merge into one cross-repo graph
/graphify <path> --mode deep                          # thorough extraction, richer INFERRED edges
/graphify <path> --update                             # incremental - re-extract only new/changed files
/graphify <path> --directed                            # build directed graph (preserves edge direction: source→target)
/graphify <path> --whisper-model medium                # use a larger Whisper model for better transcription accuracy
/graphify <path> --cluster-only                       # rerun clustering on existing graph
/graphify <path> --no-viz                             # skip visualization, just report + JSON
/graphify <path> --html                               # (HTML is generated by default - this flag is a no-op)
/graphify <path> --svg                                # also export graph.svg (embeds in Notion, GitHub)
/graphify <path> --graphml                            # export graph.graphml (Gephi, yEd)
/graphify <path> --neo4j                              # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for Neo4j
/graphify <path> --neo4j-push bolt://localhost:7687   # push directly to Neo4j
/graphify <path> --mcp                                # start MCP stdio server for agent access
/graphify <path> --watch                              # watch folder, auto-rebuild on code changes (no LLM needed)
/graphify <path> --wiki                               # build agent-crawlable wiki (index.md + one article per community)
/graphify <path> --obsidian --obsidian-dir ~/vaults/my-project  # write vault to custom path (e.g. existing vault)
/graphify add <url>                                   # fetch URL, save to ./raw, update graph
/graphify add <url> --author "Name"                   # tag who wrote it
/graphify add <url> --contributor "Name"              # tag who added it to the corpus
/graphify query "<question>"                          # BFS traversal - broad context
/graphify query "<question>" --dfs                    # DFS - trace a specific path
/graphify query "<question>" --budget 1500            # cap answer at N tokens
/graphify path "AuthModule" "Database"                # shortest path between two concepts
/graphify explain "SwinTransformer"                   # plain-language explanation of a node
```

## What graphify is for

Drop any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into graphify and get a queryable knowledge graph. Persistent across sessions, honest audit trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), community detection surfaces cross-document connections you wouldn't think to ask about.

## What You Must Do When Invoked

If the user invoked `/graphify --help` or `/graphify -h` (with no other arguments), print the contents of the `## Usage` section above verbatim and stop. Do not run any commands, do not detect files, do not default the path to `.`. Just print the Usage block and return.

If no path was given, use `.` (current directory). Do not ask the user for a path.

If the path argument starts with `https://github.com/` or `http://github.com/`, treat it as a GitHub URL - run Step 0 before anything else, then continue with the resolved local path.

Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps.

### Step 0 - Clone GitHub repo(s) (only if a GitHub URL was given)

**Single repo:**
```bash
LOCAL_PATH=$(graphify clone <github-url> [--branch <branch>])
# Use LOCAL_PATH as the target for all subsequent steps
```

# 2. Read shebang from graphify binary (pipx and direct pip installs)

fi
# 3. Fall back to python3
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ]; then PYTHON="python3"; fi
if ! "$PYTHON" -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null; then

fi

# PLAN — Local LLM ("Métis Local") in AskToto

Version: 1 (pre-attack draft)
Author: Visionary (Claude Fable 5)
Date: 2026-07-10

## 1. Goal

Add an on-device LLM provider to Métis (Electron 39, TypeScript, mac arm64 + win x64) so
lightweight, latency-critical, privacy-sensitive tasks run locally and free, while heavy
tasks keep using cloud providers:

- **Local (new):** live `suggest` (what to say next), `summary` (mid-meeting summary),
  `vision` (screenshot understanding/OCR-ish reading) — user-toggleable per task.
- **Cloud (unchanged):** `recap` (post-meeting document), `answer` (brain-grounded Q&A),
  think/deep tiers, brain/graph ingest pipeline (Opus path), follow-up artifacts.

Success metric: with a local model downloaded and a live meeting running, clicking
Suggest yields first token in ≤ 1.5 s on an M-series Mac (warm cache), with zero cloud
calls, and the existing cloud waterfall still works untouched when local is disabled or
fails.

## 2. Non-goals (v1)

- No local recap/deep-answer (quality demands cloud models).
- No change to brain/ingest.ts or graphify.ts (Opus graph pipeline reserved path).
- No Ollama/LM Studio dependency; no renderer-side inference (transformers.js/ONNX);
  no MTP/speculative decoding; no fine-tuning; no model marketplace.
- No new HTTP surface beyond loopback; the sidecar is never exposed off-device.

## 3. Research grounding (verified 2026-07-10 via web; flags where unverified)

- **Model family: Qwen3.5 small series** (released 2026-03-02): 0.8B / 2B / 4B / 9B.
  Apache 2.0, natively multimodal (text+image+video), 201 languages (French+English
  needed), 262k native context, hybrid Gated-DeltaNet + sparse-MoE architecture.
  GGUF available day-1; requires recent llama.cpp for the new operators.
  Speed refs: 0.8B ≈ 55 tok/s decode on M2 Air, ≈ 80 tok/s on M2 Max; 4B needs ≈ 2.5 GB
  at Q4. [sources: marktechpost 2026-03-02; unsloth docs; llmcheck/willitrunai benchmark
  pages; enclaveai blog]
- **edge-lm (TheStageAI): rejected.** Python+MLX, Apple-Silicon-only, Gemma-4-only —
  no Windows, no Node embedding. [github.com/TheStageAI/edge-lm README]
- **node-llama-cpp: rejected as the runtime** (kept as documented fallback): v3.19.0
  (2026-06-30) has first-class Electron support but **no vision/multimodal input** in its
  documented feature set — vision is half the ask. Also: context sequences do not share
  KV; Vulkan multi-context flaky. [node-llama-cpp.withcat.ai guide pages]
- **Chosen runtime: `llama-server` (llama.cpp) sidecar.** OpenAI-compatible
  `/v1/chat/completions` including `image_url` input with `--mmproj`; per-slot prompt
  caching with `--cache-reuse` (KV prefix reuse for a growing transcript); `--api-key`;
  `--parallel` slots. [llama.cpp tools/server README; unsloth deployment guide]
- **UNVERIFIED (must be pinned during build, not assumed):** exact GGUF repo/filenames +
  sha256 for Qwen3.5-0.8B/2B/4B instruct quants and their mmproj files (candidates:
  official Qwen HF repos, unsloth/*, AaryanK/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF); exact llama.cpp release
  tag with Qwen3.5 support and its per-platform asset names/sha256; Windows tok/s numbers;
  Qwen3.5-0.8B screenshot-OCR quality vs 2B (build includes a screenshot eval check).

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Shape

```
Electron main process
├── src/main/llm/local-runtime.ts   NEW — sidecar lifecycle
│     spawn llama-server → 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral port>, --api-key <random/session>
│     health poll /health; idle shutdown; kill on quit; crash → restart-once → cloud failover
├── src/main/llm/local-models.ts    NEW — model manifest + download/verify/delete
│     userData/local-llm/models/*.gguf (+mmproj), sha256-verified, IPC progress
├── src/main/llm/local.ts           NEW — provider strategy (thin)
│     ensure runtime up → delegate to streamOpenAI(baseURL=http://127.0.0.1:port/v1)
└── src/main/index.ts               EDIT — eligibility + mode-preference routing
src/shared/providers.ts             EDIT — ProviderId 'local', ProviderKind 'local', PROVIDERS entry (vision: true)
src/renderer (App.tsx, state.ts)    EDIT — Settings "Local AI" card
scripts/fetch-llama-server.mjs      NEW — build-time pinned runtime download (per platform)
scripts/check-llama-sidecar.mjs     NEW — packaging guard (mirrors check:ffmpeg / check:sherpa)
electron-builder.yml                EDIT — extraResources for the sidecar binaries; mac signing covers them
```

### 4.2 Why sidecar (vs node-llama-cpp addon / renderer ONNX)

1. Vision day-1 via `--mmproj` through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint — `src/main/llm/openai.ts`
   already sends screenshots as data-URI `image_url` (openai.ts:10-17) and already retries
   without `stream_options` for local endpoints that reject it (openai.ts:28-33, 110-119).
   The local strategy is therefore ~a config shim, not a new streaming client.
2. Growing-transcript latency: server-side per-slot prompt caching + `--cache-reuse`
   reuses the transcript-prefix KV across requests — no custom KV engineering.
3. Process isolation: a 1-3 GB inference runtime cannot take down the app.
4. Packaging: explicit pinned binaries via a fetch script + guard, exactly the repo's
   existing ffmpeg-sidecar pattern — avoiding the npm optional-natives cross-build trap
   this repo already fought with sherpa-onnx.

### 4.3 Provider integration (the seam)

- `ProviderKind` gains `'local'` (src/shared/providers.ts:18); `createStream` gains
  `case 'local': return streamLocal(opts)` (src/main/llm.ts:16-27).
- PROVIDERS entry: `local` — label "Métis Local · on-device", `tier: 'featured'`,
  `vision: true`, `models` = manifest ids, no key (keyHint '', keyPattern '').
- Eligibility (index.ts attempt()/pickFailover, ~1961-2062): `local` is eligible when
  the runtime binary is present AND the selected model is downloaded AND
  `settings.localLlm.enabled` — replaces the API-key check for this provider.
- Mode preference: when local is eligible and the user enabled the task
  (`localLlm.useFor.suggest|summary|vision`), `attempt('local', …)` is tried FIRST for
  modes `suggest` / `summary` / `vision` (base tier only); on any pre-token failure the
  existing failover waterfall proceeds unchanged (local → Dust/Claude/GPT…).
  think/deep tiers and `answer`/`recap` never route local in v1.
- `providerVisionOk('local')` = static true (mmproj ships with every manifest model).
- Idle budget: suggest keeps its 15 s budget (index.ts:2071-2082); local TTFT warm target
  ≤ 1.5 s makes that comfortable.
- Privacy note: `redactSecrets` (index.ts:1943) keeps running for cloud, and ALSO for
  local in v1 (defense in depth, zero behavior divergence); a later phase may relax it
  for the local path since data never leaves the device.

### 4.4 Sidecar contract

Spawn args (mac): `llama-server -m <model.gguf> --mmproj <mmproj.gguf> --host 127.0.0.1
--port <ephemeral> --api-key <32-byte random hex, per session> -c 8192 --parallel 2
--cache-reuse 256 -ngl 99 --no-webui`
Windows: same, GPU offload only when the Vulkan build initializes; CPU build fallback.
- Port: OS-assigned ephemeral (bind 0, read actual) — no fixed-port collisions.
- API key: generated per app session, held in main-process memory only, passed to the
  strategy as `opts.apiKey`. Never logged, never persisted, never sent to renderer.
- Lifecycle: start on first local request or meeting start (pre-warm); idle-stop after
  15 min without a meeting or request; SIGKILL on app quit (before-quit hook).
- Health: poll `GET /health` until 200 (timeout 30 s mac / 60 s win first-run for
  Defender scan latency); crash mid-stream → onError → waterfall failover; one automatic
  restart per 10-minute window, then local marked unavailable for the session (audit-logged).
- Pre-warm: after each transcript delta batch (debounced ~5 s) while a meeting is live and
  suggest-local is enabled, POST a 1-token completion carrying the current system+transcript
  prefix so `--cache-reuse` keeps the KV hot; click-time request then pays only the delta.

### 4.5 Model manifest + runtime provisioning

- `LOCAL_MODELS` manifest (in local-models.ts): id, label, HF download URL(s), sha256,
  bytes, minFreeRamGB, blurb. v1 entries: `qwen3.5-0.8b` (lite — Owner's pick),
  `qwen3.5-2b` (default), `qwen3.5-4b` (quality; gated to ≥ 16 GB RAM machines).
  Q4_K_M instruct quants + matching mmproj. Exact URLs+sha256 pinned during R2 from
  verified HF repos (prefer official Qwen; else unsloth) — fabricating checksums is
  forbidden; the rock's proof includes checksum verification of a real download.
- Download: HTTPS from huggingface.co with resume (Range), progress via IPC events,
  sha256 streamed during download, rejected file deleted. Storage:
  `app.getPath('userData')/local-llm/models/`.
- Runtime: `scripts/fetch-llama-server.mjs` downloads the PINNED llama.cpp release assets
  (tag + sha256 in the script) for the current build platform into `resources/llama/<platform>/`
  at package time; `scripts/check-llama-sidecar.mjs` hard-fails packaging when the binary
  for the target platform is missing (lesson: sherpa cross-build silently dropped
  win natives). electron-builder ships it under extraResources; macOS signing includes it
  (Gatekeeper-safe — a runtime downloaded at first-run would be quarantined, hence
  bundle-and-sign, not download).
- App size cost: ≈ 5-40 MB per platform (llama-server + dlls). Accepted.

### 4.6 Settings UI (renderer)

"Local AI" card in Settings (App.tsx + state.ts, following existing provider-card
patterns): enable toggle; model picker with size/RAM guidance (0.8B ≈ 0.7 GB / 2B ≈ 1.4 GB /
4B ≈ 2.5 GB downloads — final numbers from the pinned manifest); download button with
progress + cancel; delete model; three "use for" checkboxes (Live suggestions, Summaries,
Screenshots); status line (runtime running/stopped, model loaded). Renderer gets ONLY
metadata via IPC (states, progress %) — never paths, port, or api-key.

## 5. Error matrix

| Failure | Exit/signal | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| Sidecar binary missing/corrupt | spawn ENOENT / sha mismatch | local ineligible; Settings shows "runtime missing — reinstall app"; audit `local.runtime.missing` |
| Port bind race | llama-server exits non-zero | retry once with fresh ephemeral port |
| Model checksum mismatch (download) | sha256 ≠ manifest | delete file, surface "download corrupted — retry", audit `local.model.checksum_fail` |
| Model corrupt on load | server exits during load | mark model bad, prompt redownload; do NOT auto-delete without user ack |
| OOM / insufficient RAM | server exit / load fail | RAM check gates download+load (os.totalmem vs minFreeRamGB); on failure suggest smaller model |
| Sidecar crash mid-stream | stream aborts | onError → existing failover waterfall (cloud answers); one auto-restart per 10 min |
| Health timeout (Defender first-run) | no 200 in budget | win budget 60 s; then treat as crash path |
| First token > idleMs | existing watchdog (shared.ts idleWatchdog) | unchanged — failover fires |
| App quit | before-quit | SIGKILL sidecar, remove temp files |

## 6. Standards

- Repo conventions: TypeScript strict, colocated `*.test.ts` vitest, comment style =
  explain the constraint not the mechanics, `npm run typecheck` (both tsconfigs) green,
  `npm test` green.
- Security bar (repo's existing): renderer sandbox/contextIsolation untouched; no new
  IPC that leaks paths/keys; sidecar loopback-only + api-key; downloads HTTPS +
  sha256-pinned; VISION_GUARD stays on local vision turns; audit events for runtime
  start/stop/crash and model download/delete.
- No placeholder code, no TODO-stubs; every rock lands with its tests.

# appId stays com.mantu.asktoto through the Métis rebrand ON PURPOSE: macOS TCC grants (mic/screen)
# and updater identity are keyed to it — changing it would reset permissions and orphan existing
# installs. Everything user-visible says Métis; this internal id is never shown.
appId: com.mantu.asktoto
productName: Métis
# Strip OneDrive/Finder xattrs from the packed app before signing — codesign hard-rejects them
# ("resource fork … detritus not allowed"); this repo lives in CloudStorage so they're everywhere.
afterPack: scripts/after-pack.mjs
copyright: © 2026 Mantu · Métis — built by Tony Walteur
# App icon: build/icon.png (1024² Métis goddess mark) → electron-builder derives mac .icns + win .ico automatically.
# Code signing is env-driven (see SIGNING.md):
#   mac/win:  CSC_LINK (path/base64 of the .p12) + CSC_KEY_PASSWORD
#   notarize: APPLE_ID + APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD + APPLE_TEAM_ID
# NOTE (local dev builds only): do NOT add `mac.identity` or override `directories.output` here.
#   - identity: this yml is shared with CI (build.yml/release.yml), which has no signing cert —
#     pinning an identity name that doesn't exist in CI's keychain would hard-fail electron-builder there.
#   - directories.output: CI's build.yml uploads artifacts from `release/*` (see .github/workflows/build.yml);
#     changing the default here would silently break that upload step on every PR.
#   Local rebuilds that need keychain-safe signing + an OneDrive-free output dir should use
#   `npm run dist:local`, which passes both as one-off `-c` CLI overrides instead (see package.json).
directories:
  output: release
  buildResources: build
files:
  - out/**/*
  - package.json
  - '!out/**/*.map'
  - '!**/*.d.ts'
asar: true
# Native addons (.node) must live outside the asar to be loadable at runtime. sherpa-onnx-node (Parakeet
# engine) + its per-platform binary packages are unpacked here so they ship + load in the installed app.
asarUnpack:
  - '**/node_modules/sherpa-onnx-node/**'
  - '**/node_modules/sherpa-onnx-*/**'
extraResources:
  # Mantu Intelligence dashboard — static build of the intelligence/ workspace, loaded in its own
  # window (src/main/intelligence.ts). Populated by `npm run build:intelligence` before packaging.
  - from: intelligence/dist
    to: intelligence
  - from: build/managed-config.example.json
    to: managed-config.example.json
  - from: build/managed-config.enterprise.example.json
    to: managed-config.enterprise.example.json
  - from: build/icon.png
    to: icon.png
  - from: resources/graphify_runner.py
    to: graphify_runner.py
  - from: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
    to: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
  # Bundled ASR model weights — served via asr-model:// protocol (zero runtime download).
  # Populated by `npm run fetch-models` before packaging.
  - from: resources/models
    to: models
    # The 1.5 GiB WebGPU Whisper tier is an opt-in development/benchmark asset. Parakeet is the
    # primary on-device engine and whisper-base remains bundled as an offline fallback; shipping both
    # models puts a release above the GitHub asset safety gate with no import-path benefit.
    filter:
      - '**/*'
      - '!onnx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo/**'
  - from: resources/asr
    to: asr
  # Self-built LGPL FFmpeg sidecar used only for bounded-memory import decode. Target-specific binaries
  # live under their platform/arch subfolder; runtime never falls back to an arbitrary PATH executable.
  - from: resources/ffmpeg
    to: ffmpeg
  - from: resources/ort
    to: ort
mac:
  category: public.app-category.productivity
  # ASCII artifact names (see the win note below): the .app displays as Métis, the .dmg/.zip assets
  # and latest-mac.yml URLs stay accent-free.
  artifactName: Metis-${version}.${ext}
  target:

    - zip
  hardenedRuntime: true
  entitlements: build/entitlements.mac.plist
  entitlementsInherit: build/entitlements.mac.plist
  gatekeeperAssess: false
  extendInfo:
    NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Métis transcribes audio on-device to give you live AI suggestions.
    NSScreenCaptureUsageDescription: Métis captures system audio and your screen so the AI can help.
    LSUIElement: true
mas:

  # The default direct channel stays dmg/zip so enterprise customers keep the full feature set and
  # electron-updater. App Store builds are sandboxed and get updates through Apple.
  entitlements: build/entitlements.mas.plist
  entitlementsInherit: build/entitlements.mas.inherit.plist
  extendInfo:
    NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Métis transcribes audio on-device to give you live AI suggestions.
    NSScreenCaptureUsageDescription: Métis captures system audio and your screen so the AI can help.
    LSUIElement: true
masDev:
  entitlements: build/entitlements.mas.plist
  entitlementsInherit: build/entitlements.mas.inherit.plist
dmg:

  target:

  artifactName: Metis-Setup-${version}.${ext}

  backgroundColor: transparent

# FLOW: push a v* tag → CI (release.yml) builds + publishes to the public AskToto-Releases repo →
# every installed app finds the new version on launch, downloads in the background, installs on quit.
# CODE SIGNING is required for the updater to trust artifacts (see SIGNING.md):
#   mac/win      → CSC_LINK (path or base64 of the .p12) + CSC_KEY_PASSWORD
#                  (win can instead use WIN_CSC_LINK + WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD / Azure Trusted Signing)
#   mac notarize → APPLE_ID + APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD + APPLE_TEAM_ID
# Unsigned macOS zip updates will be rejected by Gatekeeper on install.
publish:
  # Updates are served from the PUBLIC AskToto-Releases repo's GitHub Releases — the app *code* repo stays
  # private, only the built binaries + latest-mac.yml are published there. The installed app checks this repo
  # on launch, downloads the new version in the background, and installs it on quit (perfect zero-click UX).
  # To cut a release: create the public repo once (gh repo create mysticalsin/AskToto-Releases --public),

  # NOTE (Métis rebrand): the feed repo keeps its old name — every installed app polls THIS repo by name,

  provider: github
  owner: mysticalsin
  repo: AskToto-Releases

  releaseType: release

## A. Product definition

**Positioning (one sentence).** Métis is a permission-based, on-device-first real-time copilot that hears your calls and sees your screen — and hands you a grounded, citable answer in under two seconds — while always showing that it's active and never hiding anything.

**Target users.** People who live inside real-time conversations and screens, where a 10-second pause to "go look it up" costs the moment:
- Client-facing pros — consultants, pre-sales/SE, account managers, customer success, recruiters, founders in pitches.
- Operators in demos / product reviews / support calls / research sessions who need to read a screen and answer fast.
- Regulated-industry teams (Mantu's bread and butter — banking, pharma, public sector) who need **on-device transcription + redaction** and can't ship raw audio to a SaaS.

**Top 5 killer use cases.**
1. **Live meeting/sales copilot** — "what do I say next?" → the exact spoken line, grounded in the last 2 minutes + your profile.
2. **Screen-aware help** — "what is this showing / draft a reply / explain this error" → vision answer on the screen you're actually looking at.
3. **Instant recap + action items** — at any point, "summarize / who owns what" → structured, copyable, owner-tagged.
4. **Answer from YOUR knowledge** — "what's our standard SLA / find this in our docs" → Dust-agent retrieval over internal knowledge, cited.
5. **Recall + resume** — search past meetings, reopen the recap + full transcript, and **resume the session** with the prior context carried forward.

**Why this is meaningfully better than Cluely-style products.**
- **On-device ASR by default** (Whisper/Parakeet, bundled offline) → lower latency, works on a plane, and the audio never has to leave the machine. Cluely-class tools stream your mic to their cloud.
- **Provider-agnostic routing** (Claude / GPT / Kimi / Dust / local CLI) instead of one locked vendor → best-latency-for-the-task, cost control, and no single point of failure.
- **Grounded + citable, not confident-and-wrong** — a grounding rail forces "cite the source or admit you can't see it," plus an explicit fact-check verdict card.
- **Editable per-mode prompts + custom modes** — the user owns the assistant's behavior; not a black box.
- **Transparent by design** — visible AI-active status, no stealth, no undetectability. We win on trust, which is the only durable moat for an always-listening tool.
- **Connect-once enterprise context** — Dust + Claude CLI + Codex CLI bind once via the OS keychain and persist; add/remove API keys freely.
- **Calm, Mantu-grade UI** — one pinned bar, an answer that grows below it, suggestions that auto-dismiss. It gets out of the way.

**What we will NOT build (trust/safety boundary).** No stealth / "undetectability" / hidden-from-the-room mode; no exam, interview, or meeting deception; no hidden or non-consensual recording; no evading the *other* participants' awareness; no OS/security-control bypass; no engagement dark patterns. Métis's content-protection only keeps the assistant's private answers out of *your own* outgoing screen-share — it is a privacy feature for the user, never a tool to deceive others. If a feature only makes sense for cheating, it doesn't ship.

## Section B — UX Design

---

### B.1 First-Run Onboarding & Permissions

Métis's onboarding is a hard gate: `settings.onboardingDone` is `false` → the full App renders nothing but `<Onboarding>` inside a `<Panel>` (`App.tsx`, near the `onboardingDone` check). It has grown from an earlier 2-step design into a **6-step walkthrough** (`Onboarding.tsx`, `step` state 1–6). No skipping — each step's `<WalkNav>` only advances forward from the current step.

**Step 1 — Consent + Identity.** The first screen shows the Mantu logo and a mandatory checkbox:

> "I will inform other participants before recording. Métis follows my company's policy and the law."

The consent checkbox (`settings.recordingConsent`) must be checked before either "Sign in with Microsoft" or "Continue without signing in" activates. Sign-in calls `window.toto.signIn()` (MSAL/Azure AD), which persists the token via `auth.ts` + safeStorage. "Continue without signing in" skips SSO but still requires the consent tick. Error copy is explicit: "Sign-in failed. Use a Mantu Microsoft account."

**Step 2 — "Ask + capture" primer.** Three `<ActionRow>` cards: Sparkles/"Ask anything" (`⌘⇧↵`), Camera/"Capture screen" (`⌘⇧S`), Zap/"Quick actions" (the four ghost-pill chips — What to say next, Fact-check, Explain, Summarize screen).

**Step 3 — Listen primer.** Three more `<ActionRow>` cards: Mic/"Listen" (transcribes both sides, suggests what to say live), FileText/"Live transcript" (toggle the rolling transcript), Plus/"New meeting" (save the current call, start fresh — see B.2's `<NewMeetingToast>`).

**Step 4 — Modes & controls primer.** Three more `<ActionRow>` cards: LayoutGrid/"Modes" (Interview, Meeting, Sales, and more), Brain/"Deep thinking" (force the strongest model, rainbow ring when on), Eye/"Show / hide" (toggle whether the window appears on a shared/recorded screen — hidden by default).

**Step 5 — Provider choice.** Routes the user to a provider in plain language: an API key path (Anthropic/Claude by default), a Dust team path, or an installed CLI path (`chooseCli()` detects whether Claude Code or Codex is actually installed on the machine, rather than assuming Claude Code, so a Codex-only install doesn't land on the wrong provider). "Decide later" is honored — recording and transcripts never require a key, so nobody is blocked here. Each choice calls `patch({ provider })` and advances to Step 6.

**Step 6 — Readiness checklist.** A live "Get ready" checklist polling `window.toto.getPermissions()` every 2,500ms while this screen is open. Rows for API key/CLI connected, Microphone, and Screen Recording — each with a green check or an amber `AlertCircle` and a one-line hint. Polling continues while the user grants permissions in System Settings, so the dots flip to green live without a reload. "Get started" calls `patch({ onboardingDone: true, onboardingDoneAt: Date.now(), recordingConsent })` and invokes `onDone()` → the App renders the full Bar.

*(Line-number citations are deliberately omitted above — `Onboarding.tsx` is 631 lines and under active development; re-derive exact locations from the `step === N` blocks and named handlers (`chooseCli`, `finish`) rather than trusting cached line numbers.)*

**Permission request timing.** Neither microphone nor screen-recording is requested at onboarding. Mic is requested the first time the user presses Listen (useListen.start → getUserMedia). Screen Recording on macOS is requested the first time `desktopCapturer` is invoked via `window.toto.capture()`. This deferral is intentional: requesting both at install forces a macOS double-permission prompt before the user has done anything; deferring to first actual use makes the request contextually obvious.

**Recovery if a permission is denied.** The checklist row stays amber and shows the hint in-line — e.g. "grant access when you first press Listen". No modal, no alert — just a persistent status the user can resolve at any time and see resolve live.

---

### B.2 Meeting / Call Mode

Meeting mode activates via `useListen.start()` → the app switches `view` to `'copilot'` and renders `<Copilot>`. The Copilot surface has three visual zones stacked vertically inside the `<Panel>`:

1. **Suggestion card** — `rounded-xl border border-[accent]/30 bg-accent-soft`. This is the primary real estate: it holds the live Assist draft or a "Press Assist for a read of the conversation, or type a question." placeholder when idle.
2. **Secondary action row** — "What to say next" and "Fact-check" as ghost pills. These are always visible; pressing either fires an LLM request immediately using the current transcript.
3. **Transcript footer** — collapsed by default ("live · N captured" + "View transcript →"). Expanding shows the speaker-bubble view (see B.6).

**No automatic meeting-detection start.** Métis does not poll window titles, browser tabs, or the calendar to auto-start Listen. That subsystem (`src/main/meeting-detect/`, `detectMeeting`/`titleMatchesCalendar`, the `onMeetingDetected` IPC push) was removed; `src/main/index.ts` has zero references to it today, and a comment at `index.ts:1301-1302` states the removal explicitly — it's the reason Accessibility permission is no longer requested at all (see I.2). `<MeetingDetectedToast>` still exists as a component file but is not imported anywhere in `App.tsx` — it is dead code, not a live UX path. Listen starts only from a deliberate user action: the `⌘⇧L` hotkey or the Bar's Listen button. `settings.autoStartOnMeeting` survives only as a vestigial zod default (`false`) in `shared/ipc.ts`, with nothing left in the main process that reads it.

**"New meeting" toast (unrelated feature, don't confuse with the above).** Pressing "New meeting" in the Bar saves the in-flight meeting and immediately starts a fresh session at 0:00 — a single click with no other visible change, easy to miss on a misclick mid-call — so `<NewMeetingToast>` (App.tsx `newMeeting()`) confirms it happened: "Previous meeting saved / New session started," auto-dismissing after 3 s. This is a confirmation toast for an explicit user action, not a detection feature.

**RecordingConsentReminder.** Fires on the start of every Listen session (if `shouldShowConsentReminder` passes): a danger-bordered banner — "Métis is listening / Other participants are being recorded. Make sure everyone has consented." This is the persistent on-screen signal that AI is active. In `requireConsentIndicator` mode (Settings toggle), it stays pinned for the whole session; otherwise it auto-dismisses after `AUTO_DISMISS_MS` and patches `lastConsentReminderAt`.

**End of call.** Pressing the listening red-dot or `⌘⇧L` again calls `endReview()`: `listen.stop()` → `view = 'review'` → fires `ask.run({ mode: 'recap', transcript })` → the `<Review>` surface streams the meeting recap into the Panel. Auto-save to the OneDrive meetings folder triggers once the recap finishes streaming (App.tsx:156-203).

### B.3 Screen-Aware Mode

Métis prewarns the screen capture the moment the input field gets focus (`Bar.tsx`: `onFocus={() => { if (props.canPrewarm) void window.toto.prewarmCapture() }}`, gated on `canPrewarm = visionAvailable && screenAsk`). By the time the user presses `⌘⇧↵`, the capture is already mid-flight — the perceived latency drops to near zero.

The routing logic in `submit()` (`App.tsx`) is a deterministic decision tree, gated on `settings.screenAsk` (a user setting, not raw vision-capability — `askScreen()` internally fails over to a vision-capable provider if the active one can't read images, or returns an actionable error if none is configured):

| State | Action |
|---|---|
| Listening (call active), empty input | `assist()` — screen + transcript combined |
| Listening, typed question | `suggest.run` with transcript context |
| Not listening, `screenAsk` on, empty input | `askScreen()` — blank Enter always means "look at my screen right now," a deliberate fresh capture |
| Not listening, `screenAsk` on, typed, an answer is already showing with no error | Plain `ask.run` (**no new capture** — the prior turn's text already describes the screen; a fresh look is one click away via Capture/`⌘⇧S`) |
| Not listening, `screenAsk` on, typed, first question of the session | `askScreen(q)` — screenshot + question together |
| Not listening, `screenAsk` off | Plain `ask.run` (typed only, no capture) |

When a screen-ask fires, the Bar shows a `contextLabel` chip ("Viewed screen") — a purple dot + Eye icon + "Viewed screen" text (Bar.tsx:153-159). This chip is a trust signal: the user can see at a glance that the answer was grounded in their screen. The same chip appears in the Answer header when `label === 'Viewed screen'` (Answer.tsx:91-108).

`desktopCapturer` output is downscaled server-side before the LLM send (VISION_MAX_EDGE) and runs entirely in `main/` — the renderer never handles raw screenshot bytes.

---

### B.4 Hotkey Flow

Registered shortcuts (main/index.ts via `globalShortcut.register`):

| Hotkey | Action | `HotkeyAction` |
|---|---|---|
| `⌘⇧↵` | Focus bar / submit ask | `'ask'` |
| `⌘⇧S` | Capture screen + ask | `'capture'` |
| `⌘⇧L` | Toggle Listen on/off | `'toggle-listen'` |
| `⌘\` | Show / hide overlay | `'hide'` |
| `⌘⇧F` | Fact-check (screen or typed claim) | `'factcheck'` |
| `⌘⇧R` | Reset / new session | `'reset'` |

**Why multi-modifier, not bare `⌘+key`.** Single-modifier shortcuts like `⌘S` or `⌘L` are owned by every app in the system. A transparent always-on overlay registering `⌘S` would intercept save-file in Figma, Chrome, and Excel — globally. Triple-modifier `⌘⇧` is rare enough that collisions in real-world apps are close to zero, while still being quick to press. The Enter key (`⌘⇧↵`) is particularly deliberate: Enter alone submits forms in whatever foreground app the user is in; `⌘⇧↵` has no standard meaning and fires only into Métis. Users learn the chord once; after that, muscle memory fires it without switching focus.

**Minimized pill safety.** If the overlay is in the `minimized` (`ControlPill`) state, every hotkey action except `'hide'` first calls `unminimize()` (App.tsx:630-632) — expanding the full widget before firing the LLM request. An LLM request fired into an unmounted Bar would produce invisible work and wasted spend. The guard is unconditional.

**Escape ladder.** Escape is not a registered global shortcut (it would break every dialog in every app). Instead it's a local keydown listener on the renderer window. Precedence cascade (App.tsx:654-684):

1. If an input/textarea has focus → blur only (never collapse while typing)
2. If minimized → expand
3. If a stream is running → cancel stream
4. If a toast/meeting prompt is open → dismiss it
5. If on a non-answer view → go back to `'answer'`
6. If not collapsed → collapse
7. If collapsed → hide

This ladder ensures a panicked Escape-mash always ends at "overlay is hidden" with no destructive side effects.

---

### B.5 Instant-Answer Overlay

The layout is a pinned-bar surface, but it is **not** a uniform "Bar-on-top, Panel-always-below" split — the current implementation branches on which view is active:

- **`view === 'answer'`** (a typed/screen ask, not a live meeting): the answer body renders **inside the Bar itself**. `App.tsx` computes `barBody = answerView && !collapsed ? body : undefined` and passes it to `<Bar body={barBody}>`; per `Bar.tsx`'s own doc comment, "when present the bar EXPANDS into one surface: big input on top, this body in the middle, and the toolbar drops to the bottom — no separate panel underneath." There is no separate `<Panel>` for this case.
- **Every other view with content** (`copilot`, `review`, `settings`, `history`, `agenda`): `isPanelBody = body != null && !answerView` is true, and that content renders in a `<Panel>` rendered below the `<Bar>` — this is the "Bar pinned, Panel grows below it" model.

A `<ControlBar>` component (`components/ControlBar.tsx`) exists in the tree for a "detached session-control pill below the panel" layout, but it is not imported or rendered anywhere in `App.tsx` today — it is dead code from an earlier design, not a live UX path. Don't design around a `detachControls`/`hideToolbar` toggle; neither exists in the current `App.tsx`.

**Quick actions are listening-only, not an idle-state row.** `<QuickActions>` (four ghost-pill shortcuts: What to say next, Fact-check, Explain, Summarize screen) renders only while `showListeningChrome` is true (`listen.listening && view !== 'review' && !stopping`) — i.e. only during an active meeting. Per the surrounding code comment, this is deliberate: "clean bar with nothing under it at launch and after a meeting ends." There is no idle-state quick-actions row before the user starts Listen or asks a question.

**Answer streaming (frame 1 → first token).** The moment `ask.run()` fires, `view = 'answer'` and `collapsed = false`. `capturing` is true during the desktopCapturer call: `<Answer text="" streaming error={null} />` renders a skeleton — three shimmer lines appear immediately, giving visual confirmation before the first token. On first token, the skeleton is replaced by the live streaming text with a pulsing accent-colored cursor.

**Resize.** `useAutoResize` (`state.ts`) calls `window.toto.setContentSize` on a `ResizeObserver` keyed to the root div. Main clamps height: `Math.max(BAR_MIN_HEIGHT, Math.min(Math.round(height), workArea.height - 48))` (`main/index.ts`), measured against the display the overlay window is actually on (not the cursor's, so a laptop + external-monitor setup of different heights doesn't clamp against the wrong screen). The window position is otherwise fixed — whichever surface is showing (embedded Bar body or separate Panel) grows toward that ceiling.

**Back arrow.** When `hasAnswer` is true and `onBack` is provided, a `ChevronLeft` appears at the far left of the input row. Pressing it calls `clearAnswer()` — clears the answer/suggestion without stopping a live session. In a live session this returns the Copilot to its idle "Press Assist" state; outside a session it resets to the idle Bar with no quick-actions row (see above).

---

### B.6 Transcript Panel

Shown inside the `<Copilot>` component's third section when `showTranscript` is true or the user presses "View transcript →".

**Speaker bubbles.** `TranscriptLine.speaker` is `'you'` or `'them'`, determined by source: mic = `'you'`, system-audio = `'them'`. No diarization model is needed. A line from you is right-aligned with `bg-accent-soft`; a line from them is left-aligned with `bg-white/[0.06]`. Each bubble carries a small uppercase label: "YOU" or "THEM" in `color-ink-3`. This mirrors a standard iMessage-like read pattern — your words are distinguishable at a glance without reading.

**Auto-scroll.** A `useEffect` on `lines` calls `scroller.scrollTop = scroller.scrollHeight` (Copilot.tsx:76-79) — the transcript always pins to the latest line as it arrives.

**Show/hide toggle.** The footer row shows "View transcript →" (chevron-right pill) while hidden; once expanded it shows "Hide transcript ↓". This is intentional: the transcript is secondary information during an active call. The primary surface is the suggestion card. Expanding the transcript is opt-in, not default, so the suggestion is never pushed off screen by a long transcript.

**Model loading state.** While `loading` is true (Whisper/Parakeet model downloading for the first time), the transcript section shows `<Spinner /> downloading speech model… N%` (using `loadingPct` from `useListen`). This is the only offline-model UX: no separate loading screen; it appears inline in the transcript area where the user would already be looking.

---

### B.7 Confidence / Citations UI

Métis currently surfaces the source of an answer via a single **context chip** in the Bar's input row and the Answer's header. The chip hierarchy:

| Source | Bar chip | Answer header |
|---|---|---|
| Screen capture | Purple dot + Eye + "Viewed screen" | Accent pill: `● Eye Viewed screen` |
| Typed question | — | Inset card with the question text |
| Fact-check | — | Inset card with "FACT-CHECK" eyebrow + claim |
| Copilot Assist + screen | "Viewed screen" (same chip) | Same pill; eyebrowLabel = "Viewed screen" |
| Copilot Assist (text only) | — | eyebrowLabel = "Assist" |

**Extending to richer provenance chips (build target).** The chip slot is already wired as a flexible `contextLabel?: string` prop on `<Bar>`. The Answer header and Copilot eyebrow both use the `label` field on `AnswerState`. To extend to timestamp / doc / web / memory chips, add these source tags to the `AnswerState.label` vocabulary, then render them as multi-chip rows in Answer.tsx and Copilot.tsx. The Bar chip is intentionally singular (space is tight); the Panel header has room for a row.

**Fact-check verdict card.** This is the most opinionated confidence UI: `Answer.tsx:parseVerdict()` reads a forced `VERDICT: <TRUE|FALSE|MISLEADING|UNVERIFIABLE>` prefix from the LLM response. TRUE = green badge, FALSE = red badge, MISLEADING = danger-tinted badge, UNVERIFIABLE = neutral. The badge renders before the bullet-point reasoning, so the user gets the verdict at a glance before reading the detail. During streaming, the raw `VERDICT:` scaffold is hidden — only "Checking…" + a pulse dot shows until the verdict word is parseable (Answer.tsx:274-278).

---

### B.8 Proactive Suggestion UI

The Assist card in Copilot is calm by design. Three controls govern when it fires:

1. **`settings.autoSuggest`** — master toggle (default `true`). If false, no proactive triggers.
2. **`settings.suggestEverySec`** — minimum interval between auto-suggestions (default 15 s). Enforced via `lastSuggestRef` (App.tsx:295-297): `if (now - lastSuggestRef.current < everyMs) return`.
3. **`settings.providerReady`** — if no provider is configured, auto-suggest is silently skipped (no error toast on every transcript line).

**Trigger.** `onQuestionRef.current` fires on each `TranscriptLine` from `useListen`. Only `speaker === 'them'` lines trigger auto-suggest (the debounce is on the listener call site — the "other person said something" event). The prompt is `ASSIST_PROMPT` + last 4,000 chars of transcript + injection guard. If the provider is vision-capable, a screen capture is appended first.

**Auto-dismiss.** Two timers run in parallel (App.tsx:236-252):
- `SUGGESTION_TTL_MS = 4000` — starts when streaming ends; dismisses `SUGGESTION_TTL_MS` after the last token.
- `SUGGESTION_MAX_MS = 7000` — starts when the suggestion ID first becomes non-null; fires unconditionally regardless of streaming state, capping a hung stream.

Together these enforce a 4–7 s window. A suggestion never lingers past 7 s from first appearance.

**Non-interruption guard.** If the user is in Settings, Review, History, or Agenda, the auto-suggest fires and completes behind the scenes, but `setView('copilot')` is not called (App.tsx:298-302). The suggestion is queued on the copilot surface ready when they return. The user's active panel is never yanked away.

**High-confidence gating (build target).** `ASSIST_PROMPT` currently does not have a confidence threshold. The model should be prompted to respond with an empty body if it does not have a useful suggestion. An empty/whitespace-only `suggest.answer.text` should suppress the card render entirely (treat it as `null`). This is the single highest-ROI change to the suggestion UX: it stops the card from appearing with weak, hedge-filled boilerplate that trains users to ignore it.

---

### B.9 Failure States

Every failure state in Métis has three elements: what it shows, the exact copy, and the recovery affordance. The `errorHint()` function in `Answer.tsx:29-38` is the existing implementation for LLM errors.

| Failure | Where it shows | Copy | Recovery affordance |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Provider not configured** | Below the Bar (App.tsx:999-1016) | "[Provider] API key" or "Connect [CLI] in Settings" | Accent CTA button → opens Settings directly |
| **Rate limit / 429** | Answer error block | "The provider is rate-limiting you. Wait a moment, or switch providers in Settings." | Retry button + Settings link in error hint |
| **Invalid / expired API key** | Answer error block | "Your API key may be invalid or expired. Update it in Settings → Your AI." | Retry + settings |
| **Timeout** | Answer error block | "The model took too long. Retry, or pick a faster tier in Settings → Thinking mode." | Retry button |
| **Network offline** | Answer error block | "Looks like a network problem. Check your connection, then retry." | Retry button |
| **Quota / billing** | Answer error block | "The provider reports a quota or billing issue. Check your account, or switch providers in Settings." | Retry |
| **Provider can't read screen** | Answer error block | "This provider can't read screens. Switch to Claude or GPT in Settings." | Retry (won't help — copy is honest) + settings |
| **Screen capture permission denied** | `captureError` state in App → Answer error | "Screen capture permission denied." (raw OS error) | `errorHint()` maps "can't read screen" → settings |
| **Mic not granted** | `listen.error` → Copilot error zone | "Microphone not available. Grant access in System Settings → Privacy → Microphone." | Copilot error zone; no button (OS settings must be opened manually) |
| **Model downloading** | Copilot transcript footer | "downloading speech model… N%" | No action needed — progress is shown |
| **Unclear audio / VAD silence** | Copilot footer when `listening && lines.length === 0` | "Waiting for speech…" | Passive — auto-resolves when audio arrives |
| **No audio yet (not listening)** | Copilot footer | "not listening" | AudioLines icon in ControlBar is the affordance |
| **Save to OneDrive failed** | Review surface, `saveError` | `saveError` raw string + retry up to 5×. After max retries: "Couldn't save automatically. Use the Save button to try again." | Manual Save button in Review footer |
| **Low confidence / unverifiable** | Fact-check UNVERIFIABLE badge | "Unverifiable" (neutral badge) + bullets explaining why | No recovery needed — verdict is final |
| **Copilot suggestion streaming stuck** | Auto-dismissed after `SUGGESTION_MAX_MS` = 7 s | Never shown — card silently clears | User can press Assist again |
| **Sign-in failed (SSO)** | Onboarding Step 1 error | "Sign-in failed. Use a Mantu Microsoft account." | Same screen; retry both buttons remain active |
| **No permission at onboarding** | Onboarding Step 2 checklist | "grant access when you first press Listen" / "needed for the other side of calls + screen capture" | Row stays amber until granted; no block on "Get started" |

**Design rule.** Failure copy names the cause and points at the exact setting to fix it. Recovery affordance is always in the same panel as the error — never a separate dialog. Error blocks are `border-danger/30 bg-danger/10 text-danger` (consistent across Answer and Review). The error hint below the raw error string is `text-[12px] text-color-ink-2` — subdued, not alarming.

---

### B.10 Useful First Answer in Under 2 s

The <2 s hotkey→useful-answer target is delivered by a chain of four overlapping UX decisions, not a single optimization:

**1. Prewarm on input focus.** `Bar.tsx`'s input `onFocus` calls `window.toto.prewarmCapture()` the moment the input is focused (gated on `canPrewarm`, i.e. a vision-capable provider and `screenAsk` on — see B.3). Main starts `desktopCapturer.getSources()` immediately. By the time `⌘⇧↵` fires, the screenshot is either already in memory or within milliseconds of completion. The user's finger hasn't left the keyboard.

**2. Immediate skeleton on submit.** `ask.run()` is synchronous on the renderer side (it sends an IPC, then sets local state). `capturing = true` → the Answer skeleton renders on the same frame as the user's keypress. There is zero blank time between action and visual feedback.

**3. Per-RAF token flushing.** `useAsk` (`state.ts`) batches stream chunks per animation frame via `requestAnimationFrame`, not per-token. This means the first visible text appears as soon as the first RAF fires after the first token arrives — typically within one 16ms frame of the IPC echo. The user sees text starting to type in under 300ms from first token.

**4. Provider routing targets speed at first token.** `shared/routing.ts` selects `tier = 'basic'` in `auto` or `never` thinking mode — the fastest non-reasoning model configured for the provider. Reasoning tiers (think/deep) are opt-in only. The `'basic'` tier is calibrated per-provider so the first token typically lands in 300–700ms. During streaming Métis shows "Thinking…" + pulse dot (Answer.tsx:243-248) only while `text === ''` — this guards the period before the first token for reasoning models like Kimi that think before responding.

**5. Sound cue on completion.** `playCue('ready')` fires on the streaming→done edge (App.tsx:262-266), gated by `settings.soundCues`. This tells the user the answer is done without them having to look. For screen questions the answer often finishes in 2–4 s total; the chime lets the user keep their eyes on the other app.

The combined effect: after `⌘⇧↵`, the overlay shows a skeleton in <50ms, first text in <300ms (network permitting), and a complete useful answer typically in 1.5–3 s for a standard screen question against Claude Sonnet or GPT-4o-mini. The <2 s first-token target is met end-to-end by the prewarm + immediate skeleton + per-RAF flush pipeline; the <2 s useful-answer target is met for fast providers on direct API (Claude, Groq, Fireworks) and degrades gracefully on heavier reasoning tiers with the Thinking… indicator.

1	# PLAN — Local LLM ("Métis Local") in AskToto
     2	
     3	Version: 1 (pre-attack draft)
     4	Author: Visionary (Claude Fable 5)
     5	Date: 2026-07-10
     6	
     7	## 1. Goal
     8	
     9	Add an on-device LLM provider to Métis (Electron 39, TypeScript, mac arm64 + win x64) so
    10	lightweight, latency-critical, privacy-sensitive tasks run locally and free, while heavy
    11	tasks keep using cloud providers:
    12	
    13	- **Local (new):** live `suggest` (what to say next), `summary` (mid-meeting summary),
    14	  `vision` (screenshot understanding/OCR-ish reading) — user-toggleable per task.
    15	- **Cloud (unchanged):** `recap` (post-meeting document), `answer` (brain-grounded Q&A),
    16	  think/deep tiers, brain/graph ingest pipeline (Opus path), follow-up artifacts.
    17	
    18	Success metric: with a local model downloaded and a live meeting running, clicking
    19	Suggest yields first token in ≤ 1.5 s on an M-series Mac (warm cache), with zero cloud
    20	calls, and the existing cloud waterfall still works untouched when local is disabled or
    21	fails.
    22	
    23	## 2. Non-goals (v1)
    24	
    25	- No local recap/deep-answer (quality demands cloud models).
    26	- No change to brain/ingest.ts or graphify.ts (Opus graph pipeline reserved path).
    27	- No Ollama/LM Studio dependency; no renderer-side inference (transformers.js/ONNX);
    28	  no MTP/speculative decoding; no fine-tuning; no model marketplace.
    29	- No new HTTP surface beyond loopback; the sidecar is never exposed off-device.
    30	
    31	## 3. Research grounding (verified 2026-07-10 via web; flags where unverified)
    32	
    33	- **Model family: Qwen3.5 small series** (released 2026-03-02): 0.8B / 2B / 4B / 9B.
    34	  Apache 2.0, natively multimodal (text+image+video), 201 languages (French+English
    35	  needed), 262k native context, hybrid Gated-DeltaNet + sparse-MoE architecture.
    36	  GGUF available day-1; requires recent llama.cpp for the new operators.
    37	  Speed refs: 0.8B ≈ 55 tok/s decode on M2 Air, ≈ 80 tok/s on M2 Max; 4B needs ≈ 2.5 GB
    38	  at Q4. [sources: marktechpost 2026-03-02; unsloth docs; llmcheck/willitrunai benchmark
    39	  pages; enclaveai blog]
    40	- **edge-lm (TheStageAI): rejected.** Python+MLX, Apple-Silicon-only, Gemma-4-only —
    41	  no Windows, no Node embedding. [github.com/TheStageAI/edge-lm README]
    42	- **node-llama-cpp: rejected as the runtime** (kept as documented fallback): v3.19.0
    43	  (2026-06-30) has first-class Electron support but **no vision/multimodal input** in its
    44	  documented feature set — vision is half the ask. Also: context sequences do not share
    45	  KV; Vulkan multi-context flaky. [node-llama-cpp.withcat.ai guide pages]
    46	- **Chosen runtime: `llama-server` (llama.cpp) sidecar.** OpenAI-compatible
    47	  `/v1/chat/completions` including `image_url` input with `--mmproj`; per-slot prompt
    48	  caching with `--cache-reuse` (KV prefix reuse for a growing transcript); `--api-key`;
    49	  `--parallel` slots. [llama.cpp tools/server README; unsloth deployment guide]
    50	- **UNVERIFIED (must be pinned during build, not assumed):** exact GGUF repo/filenames +
    51	  sha256 for Qwen3.5-0.8B/2B/4B instruct quants and their mmproj files (candidates:
    52	  official Qwen HF repos, unsloth/*, AaryanK/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF); exact llama.cpp release
    53	  tag with Qwen3.5 support and its per-platform asset names/sha256; Windows tok/s numbers;
    54	  Qwen3.5-0.8B screenshot-OCR quality vs 2B (build includes a screenshot eval check).
    55	
    56	## 4. Architecture
    57	
    58	### 4.1 Shape
    59	
    60	```
    61	Electron main process
    62	├── src/main/llm/local-runtime.ts   NEW — sidecar lifecycle
    63	│     spawn llama-server → 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral port>, --api-key <random/session>
    64	│     health poll /health; idle shutdown; kill on quit; crash → restart-once → cloud failover
    65	├── src/main/llm/local-models.ts    NEW — model manifest + download/verify/delete
    66	│     userData/local-llm/models/*.gguf (+mmproj), sha256-verified, IPC progress
    67	├── src/main/llm/local.ts           NEW — provider strategy (thin)
    68	│     ensure runtime up → delegate to streamOpenAI(baseURL=http://127.0.0.1:port/v1)
    69	└── src/main/index.ts               EDIT — eligibility + mode-preference routing
    70	src/shared/providers.ts             EDIT — ProviderId 'local', ProviderKind 'local', PROVIDERS entry (vision: true)
    71	src/renderer (App.tsx, state.ts)    EDIT — Settings "Local AI" card
    72	scripts/fetch-llama-server.mjs      NEW — build-time pinned runtime download (per platform)
    73	scripts/check-llama-sidecar.mjs     NEW — packaging guard (mirrors check:ffmpeg / check:sherpa)
    74	electron-builder.yml                EDIT — extraResources for the sidecar binaries; mac signing covers them
    75	```
    76	
    77	### 4.2 Why sidecar (vs node-llama-cpp addon / renderer ONNX)
    78	
    79	1. Vision day-1 via `--mmproj` through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint — `src/main/llm/openai.ts`
    80	   already sends screenshots as data-URI `image_url` (openai.ts:10-17) and already retries
    81	   without `stream_options` for local endpoints that reject it (openai.ts:28-33, 110-119).
    82	   The local strategy is therefore ~a config shim, not a new streaming client.
    83	2. Growing-transcript latency: server-side per-slot prompt caching + `--cache-reuse`
    84	   reuses the transcript-prefix KV across requests — no custom KV engineering.
    85	3. Process isolation: a 1-3 GB inference runtime cannot take down the app.
    86	4. Packaging: explicit pinned binaries via a fetch script + guard, exactly the repo's
    87	   existing ffmpeg-sidecar pattern — avoiding the npm optional-natives cross-build trap
    88	   this repo already fought with sherpa-onnx.
    89	
    90	### 4.3 Provider integration (the seam)
    91	
    92	- `ProviderKind` gains `'local'` (src/shared/providers.ts:18); `createStream` gains
    93	  `case 'local': return streamLocal(opts)` (src/main/llm.ts:16-27).
    94	- PROVIDERS entry: `local` — label "Métis Local · on-device", `tier: 'featured'`,
    95	  `vision: true`, `models` = manifest ids, no key (keyHint '', keyPattern '').
    96	- Eligibility (index.ts attempt()/pickFailover, ~1961-2062): `local` is eligible when
    97	  the runtime binary is present AND the selected model is downloaded AND
    98	  `settings.localLlm.enabled` — replaces the API-key check for this provider.
    99	- Mode preference: when local is eligible and the user enabled the task
   100	  (`localLlm.useFor.suggest|summary|vision`), `attempt('local', …)` is tried FIRST for
   101	  modes `suggest` / `summary` / `vision` (base tier only); on any pre-token failure the
   102	  existing failover waterfall proceeds unchanged (local → Dust/Claude/GPT…).
   103	  think/deep tiers and `answer`/`recap` never route local in v1.
   104	- `providerVisionOk('local')` = static true (mmproj ships with every manifest model).
   105	- Idle budget: suggest keeps its 15 s budget (index.ts:2071-2082); local TTFT warm target
   106	  ≤ 1.5 s makes that comfortable.
   107	- Privacy note: `redactSecrets` (index.ts:1943) keeps running for cloud, and ALSO for
   108	  local in v1 (defense in depth, zero behavior divergence); a later phase may relax it
   109	  for the local path since data never leaves the device.
   110	
   111	### 4.4 Sidecar contract
   112	
   113	Spawn args (mac): `llama-server -m <model.gguf> --mmproj <mmproj.gguf> --host 127.0.0.1
   114	--port <ephemeral> --api-key <32-byte random hex, per session> -c 8192 --parallel 2
   115	--cache-reuse 256 -ngl 99 --no-webui`
   116	Windows: same, GPU offload only when the Vulkan build initializes; CPU build fallback.
   117	- Port: OS-assigned ephemeral (bind 0, read actual) — no fixed-port collisions.
   118	- API key: generated per app session, held in main-process memory only, passed to the
   119	  strategy as `opts.apiKey`. Never logged, never persisted, never sent to renderer.
   120	- Lifecycle: start on first local request or meeting start (pre-warm); idle-stop after
   121	  15 min without a meeting or request; SIGKILL on app quit (before-quit hook).
   122	- Health: poll `GET /health` until 200 (timeout 30 s mac / 60 s win first-run for
   123	  Defender scan latency); crash mid-stream → onError → waterfall failover; one automatic
   124	  restart per 10-minute window, then local marked unavailable for the session (audit-logged).
   125	- Pre-warm: after each transcript delta batch (debounced ~5 s) while a meeting is live and
   126	  suggest-local is enabled, POST a 1-token completion carrying the current system+transcript
   127	  prefix so `--cache-reuse` keeps the KV hot; click-time request then pays only the delta.
   128	
   129	### 4.5 Model manifest + runtime provisioning
   130	
   131	- `LOCAL_MODELS` manifest (in local-models.ts): id, label, HF download URL(s), sha256,
   132	  bytes, minFreeRamGB, blurb. v1 entries: `qwen3.5-0.8b` (lite — Owner's pick),
   133	  `qwen3.5-2b` (default), `qwen3.5-4b` (quality; gated to ≥ 16 GB RAM machines).
   134	  Q4_K_M instruct quants + matching mmproj. Exact URLs+sha256 pinned during R2 from
   135	  verified HF repos (prefer official Qwen; else unsloth) — fabricating checksums is
   136	  forbidden; the rock's proof includes checksum verification of a real download.
   137	- Download: HTTPS from huggingface.co with resume (Range), progress via IPC events,
   138	  sha256 streamed during download, rejected file deleted. Storage:
   139	  `app.getPath('userData')/local-llm/models/`.
   140	- Runtime: `scripts/fetch-llama-server.mjs` downloads the PINNED llama.cpp release assets
   141	  (tag + sha256 in the script) for the current build platform into `resources/llama/<platform>/`
   142	  at package time; `scripts/check-llama-sidecar.mjs` hard-fails packaging when the binary
   143	  for the target platform is missing (lesson: sherpa cross-build silently dropped
   144	  win natives). electron-builder ships it under extraResources; macOS signing includes it
   145	  (Gatekeeper-safe — a runtime downloaded at first-run would be quarantined, hence
   146	  bundle-and-sign, not download).
   147	- App size cost: ≈ 5-40 MB per platform (llama-server + dlls). Accepted.
   148	
   149	### 4.6 Settings UI (renderer)
   150	
   151	"Local AI" card in Settings (App.tsx + state.ts, following existing provider-card
   152	patterns): enable toggle; model picker with size/RAM guidance (0.8B ≈ 0.7 GB / 2B ≈ 1.4 GB /
   153	4B ≈ 2.5 GB downloads — final numbers from the pinned manifest); download button with
   154	progress + cancel; delete model; three "use for" checkboxes (Live suggestions, Summaries,
   155	Screenshots); status line (runtime running/stopped, model loaded). Renderer gets ONLY
   156	metadata via IPC (states, progress %) — never paths, port, or api-key.
   157	
   158	## 5. Error matrix
   159	
   160	| Failure | Exit/signal | Handling |
   161	|---|---|---|
   162	| Sidecar binary missing/corrupt | spawn ENOENT / sha mismatch | local ineligible; Settings shows "runtime missing — reinstall app"; audit `local.runtime.missing` |
   163	| Port bind race | llama-server exits non-zero | retry once with fresh ephemeral port |
   164	| Model checksum mismatch (download) | sha256 ≠ manifest | delete file, surface "download corrupted — retry", audit `local.model.checksum_fail` |
   165	| Model corrupt on load | server exits during load | mark model bad, prompt redownload; do NOT auto-delete without user ack |
   166	| OOM / insufficient RAM | server exit / load fail | RAM check gates download+load (os.totalmem vs minFreeRamGB); on failure suggest smaller model |
   167	| Sidecar crash mid-stream | stream aborts | onError → existing failover waterfall (cloud answers); one auto-restart per 10 min |
   168	| Health timeout (Defender first-run) | no 200 in budget | win budget 60 s; then treat as crash path |
   169	| First token > idleMs | existing watchdog (shared.ts idleWatchdog) | unchanged — failover fires |
   170	| App quit | before-quit | SIGKILL sidecar, remove temp files |
   171	
   172	## 6. Standards
   173	
   174	- Repo conventions: TypeScript strict, colocated `*.test.ts` vitest, comment style =
   175	  explain the constraint not the mechanics, `npm run typecheck` (both tsconfigs) green,
   176	  `npm test` green.
   177	- Security bar (repo's existing): renderer sandbox/contextIsolation untouched; no new
   178	  IPC that leaks paths/keys; sidecar loopback-only + api-key; downloads HTTPS +
   179	  sha256-pinned; VISION_GUARD stays on local vision turns; audit events for runtime
   180	  start/stop/crash and model download/delete.
   181	- No placeholder code, no TODO-stubs; every rock lands with its tests.
   182	
   183	## 7. Risks
   184	
   185	1. **Qwen3.5 GGUF/mmproj availability or naming differs from expectation** → R2 starts
   186	   with a verification step; if official quants are missing, fall back to unsloth quants;
   187	   if 2B mmproj is missing, default model becomes 0.8B (which the Owner already validated
   188	   exists with llama.cpp-ecosystem quants).
   189	2. **llama.cpp pinned release regressions** → pin a tag verified to load Qwen3.5 during R1;
   190	   the fetch script makes upgrades a one-line change.
   191	3. **Windows Defender/SmartScreen slow first spawn** → 60 s health budget + status UI.
   192	4. **Suggest quality at 0.8B disappoints** → default is 2B; per-task toggles let the user
   193	   keep suggest on cloud while summaries/vision run local.
   194	5. **OneDrive checkout weirdness** (worktree already mitigated) → all build/test runs in
   195	   the local-disk worktree.
   196	
   197	## 8. Draft rocks (proof commands lock at approval)
   198	
   199	## Rock 1: Provision and manage the llama-server sidecar runtime
   200	Owner: Integrator (built by Sonnet executor under Visionary review)
   201	Due: engagement day 1
   202	Done means: pinned llama-server binaries fetch+verify at package time, spawn/health/idle/kill lifecycle works on mac arm64, packaging guard fails hard when the target platform binary is missing.

   204	Status: NOT STARTED
   205	
   206	## Rock 2: Model manifest, download, verify, delete
   207	Owner: Integrator (Sonnet executor)
   208	Due: engagement day 1
   209	Done means: manifest with ≥ 2 pinned Qwen3.5 models (real URLs + real sha256 verified by an actual download during development), resumable download with progress IPC, streamed sha256 verification, RAM gating, delete.
   210	Proof: `npm test -- local-models` → exit 0 (checksum-reject case + manifest-shape case + RAM-gate case green)
   211	Status: NOT STARTED
   212	
   213	## Rock 3: `local` provider strategy + routing integration
   214	Owner: Integrator (Sonnet executor)
   215	Due: engagement day 2
   216	Done means: ProviderKind 'local' + PROVIDERS entry + streamLocal delegating to streamOpenAI with injected loopback baseURL/api-key; eligibility + mode-preference (suggest/summary/vision, base tier only) wired into attempt()/pickFailover; failover to cloud proven; think/deep/recap/answer never route local.
   217	Proof: `npm run typecheck && npm test -- local-routing` → exit 0
   218	Status: NOT STARTED
   219	
   220	## Rock 4: Settings "Local AI" card (renderer)
   221	Owner: Integrator (Sonnet executor)
   222	Due: engagement day 2
   223	Done means: enable toggle, model picker with RAM guidance, download progress + cancel, delete, three use-for checkboxes, status line; metadata-only IPC.

A local provider with no stored key needs that readiness model updated, not just the main-process waterfall.
